facts.claim: A handle that suggests pulling creates repeated errors when the door actually requires pushing.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because the visible stimulus activates an incompatible response before reflective checking can intervene.
facts.commonError: Repeated door mistakes prove users are careless.
facts.whyWrong: The design reliably cues the wrong action across many users.

facts.claim: Paris Métro gates reduce presentation error by accepting a fare card in either orientation.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because removing a nonessential orientation requirement prevents a common slip without adding a decision.
facts.commonError: Error prevention always requires more instructions.
facts.whyWrong: The gate solves the problem by accepting more natural inputs.

facts.claim: Gmail can warn when attachment language appears in a message but no file is attached.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because the prompt targets a postcompletion error at the exact moment the sender is about to finish.
facts.commonError: A generic reminder shown when composing would be equally precise.
facts.whyWrong: The conditional warning appears only when text and file state conflict.

facts.claim: A default specifies what occurs when the chooser takes no action.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because inertia, inattention, and effort costs make nonresponse common, so the preassigned outcome receives disproportionate uptake.
facts.commonError: No default exists when a form leaves every box blank.
facts.whyWrong: The system still has a rule for nonresponse, even if that rule is no enrollment or no service.

facts.claim: Required choice is itself a form of choice architecture rather than the absence of architecture.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because the designer selects a nonresponse rule that blocks continuation until an explicit answer is supplied.
facts.commonError: Forcing an active decision is neutral because no substantive option is preselected.
facts.whyWrong: The timing, burden, and mandate to decide are designed features.

facts.claim: Prompted choice requests an answer while retaining a fallback for people who do not respond.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because the prompt increases attention without making completion depend entirely on active selection.
facts.commonError: Prompted choice and required choice are interchangeable.
facts.whyWrong: Required choice blocks nonresponse; prompted choice can preserve a default.

facts.claim: Collaborative filtering orders options using patterns from people with similar past tastes.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because shared preference data reduces a large set to items likely to map onto the user's interests.
facts.commonError: Collaborative filtering simply lists the overall most popular items.
facts.whyWrong: Its value comes from similarity-conditioned recommendations rather than one universal ranking.

facts.claim: The incentive checklist asks who chooses, who uses, who pays, and who profits.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because separating these roles reveals conflicts and hidden costs that a single price comparison misses.
facts.commonError: The chooser always bears the full cost and receives the full benefit.
facts.whyWrong: Many markets split selection, consumption, payment, and profit among different actors.

facts.claim: An incentive has less behavioral force when its cost is not salient at the moment of choice.
facts.mechanism: This mechanism operates because a delayed, bundled, or hidden charge is absent from attention when the action is evaluated.
facts.commonError: Equal economic costs always create equal behavior regardless of presentation.
facts.whyWrong: Timing and visibility determine whether the chooser mentally registers the cost.
